$comment: Read by the dev-team plugin hooks (guard.mjs / watch.mjs). Patterns are case-insensitive regexes. deny = blocked, ask = the user must confirm. Environments: test = postgres-test (localhost:5433) · development = Neon branch 'development' (backend/.env, APP_ENV=development) · production = Neon branch 'production' (Fly secrets / Infisical prod only). See TEAM.md → Hard rules.

bash.message: Port 5005 is the dev backend. Until backend/.env has been switched to the development branch (npm run env:set-dev-db, run by Nave) it talks to the REAL production database. Use the isolated e2e backend on 5006. After the switch this rule can be relaxed to 'ask'.
A Neon connection. Only the DEVELOPMENT branch may be used from here — never production. Confirm which database this command targets.
Only the isolated test DB (localhost:5433) may be opened with a SQL client.

Raw Prisma writes/Studio are blocked: they use whatever backend/.env points at. Use `npm run schema:test:push` (test DB) or `npm run schema:dev:push` (development DB — refuses unless APP_ENV=development). Production is never written from here.
`.env` files hold real secrets (DB URLs, API keys). Do not read or copy them; `.env.example` / `.env.test.example` are fine.
This script moves a database password from the clipboard into backend/.env. Nave runs it himself, in his own terminal.

This reads the REAL production schema (read-only) and needs the production URL, which should never be on this machine's everyday environment. Meant to be run by Nave at deploy time; confirm before running it from here.
Deploy goes to production (and pre-checks the live DB schema). Only with Nave's explicit go-ahead in this session.
This deletes the postgres-test data volume (test data only, but it also wipes the schema; it is rebuilt by `npm run schema:test:push`).

watch.message: Schema changed. Checklist: (1) test DB: `npm run schema:test:push` (runs automatically before `npm run test:e2e`); (2) development DB: `npm run schema:dev:push`, then restart the backend container; (3) a new @default on an existing table silently reclassifies old rows under db push — plan a backfill before production; (4) production is NOT updated by deploy: `db push` there needs Nave's explicit approval, and the schema gate in deploy.sh (`schema:check:prod`, needs PROD_DATABASE_URL) fails the deploy until it is done.
Deploy configuration changed. Keep the schema gate (`schema:check:prod`) before any `fly deploy` in deploy.sh.
